I can't point you to a specific model from these search results. They cover the airline rules, not product reviews, and I don't have verified buy links. I can tell you what to look for, so any power bank you pick will be allowed on board.

**What to look for**
- **Capacity of 100 Wh or less.** The FAA limits spare lithium-ion batteries and power banks to 100 Wh each ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries)). Look for the Wh rating printed on the unit. If it isn't, multiply volts by amp-hours. For mAh, divide by 1000 and multiply by the voltage ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries)). Using the usual 3.7 V cell rating, that works out to roughly 27,000 mAh at most. A 10,000 or 20,000 mAh bank is comfortably under the limit.
- **A clearly marked Wh rating.** This makes it easy to show a gate agent or security officer.
- **No damage and no recalls.** Damaged or recalled batteries can't fly ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7)).

**Rules to know**
- Power banks go in carry-on only, never checked bags. If your carry-on gets gate-checked, take the power bank out and keep it with you ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7)).
- Protect the terminals from short circuits. Keep it in its retail packaging, tape the terminals, or use a pouch or case ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7)).
- Airlines can be stricter than the FAA ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries)). For example, Southwest now limits each customer to **one** power bank as of April 20, 2026. It can't be in the overhead bin, can't be charged from in-seat power, and must be visible when in use ([Southwest](https://support.southwest.com/helpcenter/article/Traveling-with-lithium-batteries-e-cigarettes-and-lighters)).

**My suggestion:** Get one 10,000-20,000 mAh bank with the Wh rating printed on it. That covers a phone for several charges, stays under every airline's 100 Wh cap, and works if your airline allows only one. Check your airline's policy before you fly.

If you tell me your budget, which devices you need to charge, and which airline you're flying, I can search for specific models and give you buy links.
